![Context File Splitter Banner](assets/banner.jpg) # Context File Splitter **AI-Powered Documentation Decomposer for Clean Separation of Business Logic and System Architecture** [![Plugin: Antigravity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Antigravity-Plugin-6366f1?style=for-the-badge)](plugin.json) [![Python 3.8+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.8%2B-3776ab?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white)](split_doc.py) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-10b981?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE)
--- ## Overview In real-world software projects, documentation and AI context files tend to mix **what the business requires** (pricing tiers, approval thresholds, domain invariants) with **how the system implements it** (REST endpoints, database schemas, Redis caches, Kafka topics). **Context File Splitter** is an Antigravity plugin and CLI toolkit that automatically segments Markdown documentation, classifies every paragraph or code block using a deterministic domain-vs-technology decision rule, and assembles two clean, cross-referenced documentation trees: - **`business_logic/`** — pure domain rules, workflows, roles, permissions, and invariants free of implementation noise. - **`architecture/`** — technical contracts, APIs, data stores, infrastructure, and non-functional requirements. --- ## Business Value & Use Cases | Stakeholder / Scenario | Problem with Monolithic Docs | How Context File Splitter Solves It | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Product Owners & Domain Experts** | Business rules are buried inside SQL schemas, HTTP status codes, and JSON payloads, making review slow and error-prone. | Generates a clean `business_logic/` tree containing only technology-agnostic domain specifications that stakeholders can audit directly. | | **Software Architects & Developers** | Architectural constraints and API contracts are scattered across narrative product specs. | Extracts a dedicated `architecture/` tree with full traceability (``) back to the source requirements. | | **AI Coding Agents & LLM Context** | Feeding mixed documentation into an agent wastes context tokens and causes technology details to leak into domain models. | Provides targeted, high-signal context files—pass `business_logic/` when designing domain services and `architecture/` when building adapters or infrastructure. | | **System Migrations & Rewrites** | Replacing a tech stack (e.g., REST to gRPC, PostgreSQL to Event Sourcing) requires untangling invariant business rules from legacy implementation details. | Applies the core test: *"Would this statement remain true after a complete change of technology?"*—preserving 100% of business invariants during migrations. | --- ## How It Works The pipeline operates in four deterministic stages without ever modifying your original `src/*.md` files: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Input["1. Source Docs"] SRC["src/*.md"] end subgraph Segment["2. Segmentation"] SEG["split_doc.py segment"] UNITS["work/NN.units.json"] TOTAG["work/NN.to_tag.json"] end subgraph Classify["3. AI Classification"] PROMPT["prompt_tagging.md"] TAGS["work/NN.tags.json"] end subgraph Output["4. Assembly & Validation"] ASM["split_doc.py assemble"] CHK["split_doc.py check"] BL["business_logic/*.md"] AR["architecture/*.md"] end SRC --> SEG SEG --> UNITS SEG --> TOTAG TOTAG --> PROMPT PROMPT --> TAGS UNITS --> ASM TAGS --> ASM ASM --> BL ASM --> AR BL --> CHK AR --> CHK ``` --- ## Classification Model Every non-heading block is evaluated against the **Technology Replacement Rule** defined in [`prompt_tagging.md`](prompt_tagging.md): > **Decision Rule:** *Would the statement remain true after a complete change of technology?* > - **Yes** → `BL` (Business Logic) > - **No** → `ARCH` (Architecture) > - **Partly yes, partly no** → `MIXED` (Split into technology-free `bl_text` and implementation-focused `arch_text`) ### Example Transformation (`MIXED` Unit) **Source (`src/01_orders.md`):** ```markdown ## Approval Process Orders above 1000 PLN require approval; endpoint POST /orders/{id}/approve returns 403 for other roles. ``` **Generated Business Logic (`business_logic/01_orders.md`):** ```markdown ## Approval Process Orders above 1000 PLN require approval by an authorized role; other roles cannot approve them. ``` **Generated Architecture (`architecture/01_orders.md`):** ```markdown ## Approval Process Endpoint POST /orders/{id}/approve returns 403 for roles other than the authorized one. ``` --- ## Technical Details ### 1. Structure-Aware Markdown Segmentation (`segment`) - Parses headings (`#` through `######`) into a hierarchical stack (`Orders > Approval Process`) attached as `heading_path` metadata to every block, giving the classifier full structural context even for short paragraphs. - Preserves fenced code blocks (` ``` ` and `~~~` of any length `>= 3`) intact as single atomic units so internal blank lines or `#` comments inside code are never misinterpreted as Markdown headings. - Assigns deterministic, human-readable unit IDs (`F01-U001`, `F01-U002`, ...) across alphabetically sorted files. ### 2. Smart Heading Pruning & Cross-Referencing (`assemble`) - Buffers section headings on a hierarchy stack (`pending_bl`, `pending_ar`) and **only emits headings that contain at least one classified block** (directly or in a nested subsection). Sections that are purely architectural never leave empty orphan headings in `business_logic/`, and vice versa. - Injects HTML traceability comments (``) and bidirectional cross-links (``) for `MIXED` units. ### 3. Automated Quality & Purity Gate (`check`) - **Completeness Verification:** Ensures every block ID from `work/NN.units.json` is classified in `work/NN.tags.json`, uses a valid tag (`BL`, `ARCH`, `MIXED`), and is present in the assembled output files (requiring both `business_logic/` and `architecture/` entries for `MIXED` units). - **Domain Purity Scanner:** Scans `business_logic/*.md` using split case-sensitive (`REST`, `API`, `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `SQL`, `JSON`, `HTTP/HTTPS`, `gRPC`) and case-insensitive (`GraphQL`, `endpoint*`, `Kafka`, `Redis`, `microservice*`, `Docker`, `Kubernetes`, `queue`, `schema`, `cache*`) regular expressions to guarantee no technical jargon leaked into business documentation. - **Confidence Auditing:** Flags any unit with `confidence < 0.7` for human review and exits with a non-zero status code (`1`) if any validation problem is detected. --- ## Getting Started & Usage ### Prerequisites - **Python 3.8+** (uses only the Python standard library—no third-party packages required). - **Antigravity** (when running as an automated agent skill). ### Option A: Automated Execution via Antigravity Skill (Recommended) 1. In your target project root, place the Markdown documents you want to split inside the `src/` directory: ```text my-project/ └── src/ ├── 01_orders.md └── 02_payments.md ``` 2. Invoke the **`context-file-splitter`** skill in Antigravity (defined in [`skills/context-file-splitter/SKILL.md`](skills/context-file-splitter/SKILL.md)). 3. The agent automatically runs segmentation, classifies all blocks according to [`prompt_tagging.md`](prompt_tagging.md), assembles `business_logic/` and `architecture/`, validates output purity with `check`, and reports a summary along with any low-confidence units. ### Option B: Manual CLI Execution Run [`split_doc.py`](split_doc.py) from your target project root: ```sh # 1. Segment src/*.md into work/NN.units.json and work/NN.to_tag.json python3 /path/to/ContextFileSplitter/split_doc.py segment # 2. Classify each work/NN.to_tag.json into work/NN.tags.json # following the schema and rules in prompt_tagging.md # 3. Assemble business_logic/*.md and architecture/*.md python3 /path/to/ContextFileSplitter/split_doc.py assemble # 4. Validate completeness, MIXED links, and business logic purity python3 /path/to/ContextFileSplitter/split_doc.py check ``` --- ## Repository & Output Structure ```text ContextFileSplitter/ ├── assets/ │ └── banner.jpg # Repository hero graphic ├── skills/ │ └── context-file-splitter/ │ └── SKILL.md # Antigravity skill workflow instructions ├── plugin.json # Antigravity plugin manifest ├── prompt_tagging.md # Classification rules, schema & boundary examples ├── split_doc.py # Segmentation, assembly & validation CLI ├── README.md # Documentation └── LICENSE # Apache-2.0 License ``` When executed in a target project, the tool produces: ```text target-project/ ├── src/ # Original Markdown files (read-only, never modified) ├── work/ # Intermediate JSON artifacts (NN.units.json, NN.to_tag.json, NN.tags.json) ├── business_logic/ # Assembled technology-agnostic domain documentation └── architecture/ # Assembled technical & architectural documentation ``` --- ## License Distributed under the **Apache License 2.0**. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) for full details.
